question: advisor round-5 point 7b: physics-informed vs data-driven training principle
metric: per-component relative L2 on the held-out set, Tables 5/11's definition

physics_informed.optimizer: Adam lr=2e-3 wd=0.0, x0.9 every 1000 epochs

data_driven_matched_optimizer.optimizer: Adam lr=2e-3 wd=0.0, matched to the PI run
data_driven_matched_optimizer.note: the clean comparison: only the loss differs

data_driven_own_optimizer.note: confounded: a better optimizer AND a different loss. Best was the FINAL step, so it had not converged -- 0.0826 is a lower bound on this recipe, not its ceiling.

findings.matched: under the same optimizer the physics-informed model is 36% more accurate (0.0959 vs 0.1307). The data-driven advantage seen in the first run came from the optimizer, not the loss.
findings.unmatched: each under its own preferred recipe, the data-driven model is 16% more accurate (0.0826 vs 0.0959).
findings.label_cost: the data-driven model additionally requires 800 FEM solves = 5.65 h of CPU at Table 4a's measured rate, which the physics-informed model does not pay at all. This is independent of the optimizer.
findings.missing_cell: the 2x2 is incomplete. Physics-informed under AdamW+OneCycleLR has NOT been measured. Until it is, the strongest defensible claim is the matched one; the unmatched pair compares each method under a different recipe and cannot rank the principles.

next_run_that_would_settle_it.what: train the physics-informed model with AdamW lr=1e-3 wd=1e-5 + OneCycleLR, same 75,000 steps
next_run_that_would_settle_it.why: fills the missing cell. If it beats 0.0826 the physics-informed principle wins under both recipes; if not, the ranking depends on the recipe and must be reported as such.
